Items.Authors: Lingling Wang, Jinqing Wang
Items.Title: An investigation into the correlation between signal path variation and structural deformation in large radio telescopes

Items.Authors: Manjunath Bestha, Sivarani Thirupathi, Athira Unni
Items.Title: An observational study of systematics affecting low-resolution multi-object transmission spectroscopy
Items.Abstract: Ground-based multi-object low-resolution transmission spectroscopy (Mo-LRTS) is a commonly used method to study exoplanet atmospheres. However, these observations are affected by several time-variable systematics, such as differential slit losses, colour-dependent seeing, guiding jitter, and variations in atmospheric transparency, as well as instrumental effects like wavelength drift, flexure, and trace instability. Using HFOSC-HCT data, we investigate how these effects influence the extracted light curves and transmission spectra. Differential shifts between the program and reference stars can create or hide apparent transit features, while small wavelength misalignments can bias low-resolution spectra. We explore mitigation strategies, improved extraction methods, and common-mode corrections. This work demonstrates that modelling and correcting systematics are crucial for obtaining reliable exoplanet atmosphere measurements from ground-based Mo-LRTS using HFOSC.

Items.Authors: Thomas R. Swindle, Erik Small, David Zeleniak, Zach Gazak, Justin Fletcher
Items.Title: An open-source observatory control application for space domain awareness and time-domain astronomy
Items.Abstract: SensorKit is an autonomous observatory control system designed for satellite tracking and follow-up of rapid astronomical transients. A high-level agent built on NATS JetStream coordinates tasking, scheduling, hardware control, data processing, and other services for distributed, low-latency operation across potentially volatile environments. By default, SensorKit communicates with leading device platforms including PlaneWave PWI4, TheSkyX, ASCOM Alpaca, and INDI, with others easily added. It executes tasks based on safety, weather, viewing geometry, and user-defined constraints and provides microservices for autofocus, autoguiding, mount-model updates, and other standard observatory routines. Its central `program` layer supports communication with the US Space Force MACHINA program for space domain awareness (see these proceedings), the Unified Data Library, and provides an API for custom tasking or data-delivery pipelines. All software is open-source and hosted on github and PyPi.

Items.Authors: Shao Qi
Items.Title: An Open-Source, Cross-Platform Architecture for Autonomous Observatory Control: A Native Alpaca Implementation with an Integrated ASCOM-COM Bridge
Items.Abstract: The transition to modern, cross-platform observatory control is hindered by the prevalence of the Windows-only ASCOM COM architecture. We present a novel, open-source control system designed to bridge this gap. Our architecture features a native ASCOM Alpaca implementation in Python, enabling true OS independence. Its core innovation is an integrated, bi-directional ASCOM-COM-to-Alpaca bridge, providing seamless backward compatibility with the vast ecosystem of legacy devices. This work offers a powerful sequencing engine and an architectural blueprint that solves the protocol adoption challenge, enabling flexible, network-native, and autonomous control for the wider astronomical community.

Items.Authors: Yigit Dallilar, Vipin Kumar, Michael Wiest, Lucas Labadie, Adhirath Deshmukh, Margo Gassmueller, Roy van Boekel, Emilie Bouzerand, Wolfgang Brandner, Dennis Dolkens, Adrian Glauser, Sander Kwast, Dirk Lesman, Mirka Maresca, Wim Pessemier, Gert Raskin, Christian Straubmeier, Remko Stuik, Niels Tromp, Felix Bettonvil, Bernhard Brandl
Items.Title: An overview of the as-built subassemblies and components of WCU subsystem of METIS with a focus on the full subsystem integration
Items.Abstract: Following the finalization of its subassemblies and the full subsystem integration starting in 2026, we provide an overlook to the finalized subassemblies of the WCU subsystem of METIS and the full subsystem integration efforts along with the lessons learned therein. The as-built status and features of its core components will be discussed. This is complemented with the further discussion on the subsystem integration activities along with support equipment facilitating the integration and handling of the WCU and its components and the final performance of the WCU.

Items.Title: An overview of the stray light findings and interpretation during the LSSTCam commissioning on-sky
Items.Abstract: Wide-field telescopes such as the Vera C. Rubin are intrinsically difficult to shield from some unwanted stray and scattered light. The paper distills the experience of the Rubin commissioning for what concerns the stray light investigations, modeling, and mitigation in a wide system perspective embracing optical design, engineering, and commissioning aspects of the newest, large ground-based facility for astronomy.

Items.Authors: Elisa Radjabou, Damien Prêle, Manuel Gonzalez, Shawn Henderson, Brianna Cantrall
Items.Title: Analytical Modeling of TES Noise : Transfer Functions Across the Superconducting Transition
Items.Abstract: This work addresses the critical need to characterize detector noise for future cosmology experiments focused on measuring the B-mode signal of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB). Like many CMB observatories, the model is based on Transition-Edge Sensors (TES) and SQUID-based Time-Domain Multiplexing (TDM) readout technology.  We present a new formalism developing transfer functions for phonon, TES, and shunt resistance current noises, clearly showing their characteristic frequencies. This formulation enables the prediction of total and individual noise shapes, comparison with measurements, and direct calculation of key parameters such as cut-off frequencies and maximum amplitude spectral density values. The analysis also examines how current noise amplitude behaves at various working points within the superconducting transition.

Items.Authors: Christophe Giordano, Aziz Ziad, Alessandro Aresta, Eric Aristidi, Christophe Bailet, Chiara Bertolin, Marcel Carbillet, Yan Caujolle, Stefano Cavazzani, Clémence Edouard, Yenny Gonzalez-Ramos, Abdanour Irbah, Arnaud Le Kernec, Olivier Liandrat, Nicolas Pascal, Alvaro-Jose Pascual-Garcia, Jérôme Riedi, Nicolas Schmutz, Stéphane Victori
Items.Title: ANAtOLIA: from first light to multi-site atmospheric characterization
Items.Abstract: Atmospheric turbulence, clouds, and aerosols limit astronomical observations and the availability of optical ground stations. The ANAtOLIA project, funded by ESA, was developed to address these limitations by providing an autonomous atmospheric monitoring station. The ANAtOLIA station combines three complementary instruments: the GMT turbulence monitor, the Sky Insight all-sky camera for clouds measurements, and the Cimel CE318-T photometer for aerosols characterization. Since 2023, four stations have been deployed at four European sites (Calern, Cebreros, Catania, and Sintra) to perform a 2-year measurement campaign. This paper presents an overview of ANAtOLIA station, its operation, and the statistical results obtained across the four sites, including inter-comparisons in terms of turbulence, clouds and aerosols. The ANAtOLIA station demonstrated its efficiency as a high-performance platform for site qualification and the optimization of optical links and astronomical observations.

Items.Authors: Edoardo Maria Alberto Redaelli, Matteo Aliverti, Igor Coretti
Items.Title: ANDES @ ELT: Thermo-Electro-Mechanical budget and architecture
Items.Abstract: The ANDES instrument is progressing toward its Preliminary Design Review (PDR), and both the overall architecture and the associated budgets have now reached a consolidated level of definition. This proceeding presents the current system architecture, highlighting the main design drivers and the constraints that shape the instrument’s development.  Emphasis is placed on the thermo–electro–mechanical budget, detailing how thermal stability, electrical routing, structural performance, and subsystem interactions influence the layout and the mechanical concept. The analysis includes the identification of critical interfaces, key performance limitations, and the trade-offs adopted to comply with both scientific and engineering requirements.  This work provides an overview of the rationale behind the architectural choices and outlines the challenges that ANDES faces as it moves toward the next phases of the ELT development cycle.

Items.Authors: Lorenzo Cabona, Marcello Scalera, Alessio Zanutta, Igor Coretti, Edoardo Redaelli, Chiara Selmi, Matteo Aliverti, Ernesto Oliva, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Alessandro Marconi
Items.Title: ANDES, the high resolution spectrograph for the ELT: MBSE-based interface management
Items.Abstract: Clear identification and management of interfaces are key to the success of complex systems like ANDES Spectrograph. This contribution presents the methodological approach adopted by the ANDES System Team to ensure technical consistency, completeness, and traceability throughout the system development lifecycle. Interface management encompasses both internal and external interfaces. The Model-Based Interface Management approach implemented for ANDES ensures robust configuration control, full synchronization between interface definitions and the system architecture, and complete bidirectional traceability across all levels of the system hierarchy. Interfaces are represented within a structured hierarchy of Interfaces, Interface Channels, and Interface Ends, capturing the logical and physical interaction points between subsystems. The ANDES methodology shows how an MBSE-driven interface framework improves consistency, traceability, and verification in complex instrument development.

Items.Authors: Chiara Selmi, Alessio Zanutta, Marcello Agostino Scalera, Edoardo Maria Alberto Redaelli, Giorgio Pariani, Matteo Aliverti, Igor Coretti, Marco Landoni, Marco Riva, Ernesto Oliva, Lorenzo Cabona, Enrico Giro, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Alessandro Marconi
Items.Title: ANDES, the high resolution spectrograph for the ELT: optimization of system requirements management in view of the preliminary design review
Items.Abstract: This work outlines the optimized System Requirements Management methodology implemented for the ANDES Project as it approaches its Preliminary Design Review (PDR) in early 2026. Requirements are formally tracked and maintained using Cameo Systems Modeler, applying an MBSE framework to guarantee structural integrity and robust design element interconnection. Dynamic collaboration with subsystem teams is facilitated through.

Items.Authors: José A. Araiza-Durán, Anna Brucalassi, Andrea Tozzi, Ernesto Oliva, Debora Ferruzzi, Paolo Picchi, Alen Khanbekyan, Davide Savio, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Alessandro Marconi, Alessio Zanutta, Matteo Aliverti, Matteo Genoni, Marco Riva, Giorgio Pariani, Monica Rainer, Graham J. Murray, Nikolai Piskunov, Eric Stempels, Marcello Scalera
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: a subsystem-driven tolerance and alignment framework for the IFU derotator
Items.Abstract: The ANDES IFU includes a highly sensitive derotator subassembly whose behavior strongly affects pupil stability, alignment, and overall optical performance. We present a subsystem-level tolerance analysis focused on the derotator, combining detailed Zemax OpticStudio simulations with automated Python pipelines developed using ZOS-API. The study characterizes how derotator perturbations propagate to the pupil conjugate at the ADC and to the Viewer configuration, providing quantitative insight into focus shifts, pupil motion, and beam stability under controlled perturbations. These results form the foundation for a modular and scalable tolerance framework for the complete IFU and guide the next steps toward global system optimization.

Items.Authors: Philipp Huke, Léa Bonhomme, Christopher Broeg, Isabelle Boisse, Kamalesh Dadi, Michael Debus, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Omar Gabella, Wolfgang Gaessler, Enrico Giro, Jörg Knoche, Viljon Sekseni, Miriam Juliana Brandt, Michael Lehmitz, Jochen Liske, Madhusudan Malve, Piotr Maslowski, Richard McCracken, Christoph Mordasini, Derryck Reid, Ansgar Reiners, Sebastian Schäfer, Mirsad Sarajlic, Joackim Defigueirdo, Cheng Yuk Shan, Alessio Zanutta, Jennifer Zimara
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: calibration unit(s)
Items.Abstract: The instrumentation plan for the ELT foresees the ArmazoNes high Dispersion Echelle Spectrograph (ANDES).  All subsystems of the ANDES-project underwent internal subsystems- preliminary design reviews (ssPDR). The systems-level PDR is scheduled for mid 2026 concluding  phase B. Even though the ANDES-spectrograph is designed for maximum intrinsic stability, calibration and thus a  calibration unit (CU) is mandatory. To allow for installation at different places at the ELT (Coudé-room,  intermediate Nasmyth-platform) the CU mirrors the spectrographs design with three independent units. The  design of the individual CU is condensed by now to a high level of detail and ready for the next milestone, the  systems PDR. Here, we show the managerial part of the CU, regarding team and timeline, the engineering design  of one CU (RIZ) and outline the next steps in each element of the CU towards the Final Design Review  and the following Manufacturing, Assembly, Integration and Testing (MAIT) in Europe.

Items.Authors: Vinooja Thurairethinam, David Lee, Étienne Artigau, Frédérique Baron, Ciaran Breen, Bella Boyd, Denis Brousseau, David F. Buscher, Neil J. Cook, René Doyon, Martin Fisher, Bradley Frank, Vincent Geers, Rory Gillespie, Oscar Gonzalez, Wei Li, Lison Malo, Roberto Maiolino, David Montgomery, Alan O’Brien, Jonathan St-Antoine, James Stevenson, Simon Thibault, Philippe Vallée, Chris Waring, Sandi Wilson, Junyi Zhou, Paolo Di Marcantonio
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: design and performance analysis of the YJH spectrograph
Items.Abstract: The ArmazoNes high Dispersion Echelle Spectrograph (ANDES) is a powerful first-generation, high-resolution spectroscopic instrument for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). The UBV, RIZ, and YJH modules comprise the three fibre-fed spectrographs of the ANDES baseline design and will offer a minimum continuous wavelength coverage of 0.4-1.8µm, with a goal of being extended to 0.35-2.4µm. Coupled with a spectral resolution of ~100,000, ANDES must deliver the required wavelength calibration stability of 1 m/s over 24 hours, with a goal of 0.02 m/s across 10 years.   These requirements establish the framework for the infrared module of ANDES, the YJH Spectrograph, leading to what will likely be the largest cryogenic, ultra-stable, high-resolution spectrograph ever built. We present the current design and performance analysis of the ANDES YJH Spectrograph, outlining the engineering challenges encountered alongside the corresponding strategies adopted to navigate them.

Items.Authors: Michael Debus, Sebastian Schäfer, Philipp Huke, Ansgar Reiners
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: designing the Fabry-Perot etalon calibration light sources
Items.Abstract: The Fabry-Perot (FP) calibration light sources for ANDES have to comply to a number of design constraints, above all a requirement on the stability of accuracy of 10 cm/s over 24 hours. In addition, the large fiber size required for ANDES in turn requires a rather large etendue to be filled by the FP light sources in order to avoid causing spurious RV shifts due to insufficient scrambling. In order to maintain a sufficient effective finesse of the FP the etendue has to be constrained. We show the FP design that was presented at sub-system PDR and how it answers to these design constraints.  In addition we also explore a high finesse FP design option to aid in PSF determination, where we assume sufficient scrambling can be achieved even with smaller fibers and describe the consequences for the light source selection. Furthermore, the impacts of an extension to the U-Band as well as a possible move of the calibration unit to the intermediate Nasmyth-platform of the ELT are discussed.

Items.Authors: Arto S. Järvinen, Bruno Chazelas, Michael Weber, Daniel P. Sablowski, Tobias Schmidt
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: exposure meters for UBV and RIZ spectrographs
Items.Abstract: ANDES (ArmazoNes high Dispersion Echelle Spectrograph) is the high-resolution, fiber fed spectrograph fore-  seen to be installed as a second-generation instrument on the upcoming ELT (Extremely Large Telescope). The  main requirement necessitating an exposure meter (EM) is to provide means to measuring the mean time of  exposure (MTE) with an accuracy of 1 second. The MTE measurement is a proxy to measure the average  Barycentric Earth Radial Velocity (BERV) correction during an exposure. To provide an accurate measurement  of the BERV correction, the colour dependency of MTE must be measured.  The UBV and RIZ Exposure Meters receive its light from the Fiber-to-Fiber interface's single  large fiber which is coupled to multiple smaller fibers packed in a hexagonal pattern. The EM receives 6% of the light not be available to the spectrographs. Here we present the efficiency computations of the system, optical and optomechanical designs, the detector selection process, and control system.

Items.Authors: Wolfgang Gaessler, Santiago Barboza, Frederique Baron, Wolfgang Brandner, Vincent Benz, Paolo Di Marcantonio, René Doyon, Monica Ebert, Adrian Kaminski, Heidi Korhonen, Laura Kreidberg, Werner Laun, Michael Lehmitz, Alessandro Marconi, Paul Mollière, Andreas Quirrenbach, Ralf-Rainer Rohloff, Walter Seifert, Julian Stuermer, Wenli Xu, Alessio Zanutta
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: K-band spectrograph options
Items.Abstract: ANDES is a fiber fed high resolution spectrograph for the ELT, with the goal of providing simultaneous spectra of R~100000 over a wavelength range from 0.35 to 2.4 micron. The project is just finishing Phase-B with the system PDR.  The work on ANDES-K started with Phase-B. The feasibility to extend the baseline wavelength range from 1.8 to 2.4 micron was studied. Fiber throughput losses are higher in K than in other bands, why ANDES-K is placed close to the focal plane, which is putting limits to mass and volume. Due to such constraints, a spectrograph operating at the diffraction limit of the ELT was investigated. PDR of ANDES-K was hold November 2024 and passed successfully. The design is based on few mode fibers. We thoroughly studied the impact of modal noise created by such fibers and how to mitigate. We also developed a single mode fiber alternative. We will summarize our findings, compare existing spectrographs with our approach and finally conclude on the best option of ANDES-K.

Items.Authors: Nicolò Azzaroli, Enrico Pinna, Chiara Selmi, Edoardo Redaelli
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: optical design and analysis of the Single Conjugate Adaptive Optics (SCAO) WFS
Items.Abstract: The ANDES (ArmazoNes high Dispersion Echelle Spectrograph) instrument for the ELT includes a complex Single Conjugate Adaptive Optics (SCAO) subsystem for real-time correction of atmospheric wavefront aberrations. This paper describes the SCAO optical design, featuring a common interface arm, a dual-pair Amici Atmospheric Dispersion Corrector, and a high-order pyramid wavefront sensor with auxiliary technical and phasing channels. Sensitivity analyses for component fabrication are detailed, focusing on the pyramid assembly and main optical arm. Key AIV tolerance results quantify how misalignments affect Residual WaveFront Error and PSF/Pupil shifts, defining robust positioning tolerances and confirming compliance with top-level requirements.

Items.Authors: Giorgio Pariani, Luca Oggioni, Ernesto Oliva, Marcello Scalera, Monica Rainer, Alessio Zanutta, Paolo Di Marcantonio
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: optical design and performance estimation of the Fiber Routing subsystem
Items.Abstract: The Fiber Routing (FR) subsystem of ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph of the ELT, transfers, scrambles, and reformats the scientific and calibration light from the Front End to the spectrographs, ensuring étendue conservation, illumination stability and high throughput.  We will describe the FR optical design, which followed a process combining first-order modelling, tolerance analysis, and non-sequential simulations. We will show the details of the double scrambler, based on a ball lens, of the pupil slicer, based on a collimator and a micro-lenses array feeding a bundle of small fibers, and of the spectrometer slit, made of a linear array of fibers and micro-lenses. We will also present the full transmission budget —accounting for fiber attenuation, coatings, geometry transitions, and tolerances— across UBV, RIZ, and YJH bands.

Items.Authors: Philippe Bério, Christophe Bailet, Yan Caujolle, Gaël Chauvin, Andrea Chiavassa, Salvador Cuevas, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Omar Gabella, Patrice Martinez, Mamadou N'Diaye, Enrico Pinna, Julia Seidel, Chiara Selmi, Adrien Simonnin, Alain Spang, Edoardo Maria Alberto Redaelli
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: opto-mechanical design of the coronagraph
Items.Abstract: The ANDES coronagraph is a key subsystem of ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ESO   ELT. Developed in the SCAO sub-system, the coronagraph aims to enhance ANDES’s capability for high-contrast spectroscopy of exoplanets in reflected light, enabling the detection of temperate and rocky exoplanet atmospheres.  The coronagraph optical design is fully refractive. It includes two main arms: a science arm equipped with a Lyot-type coronagraph, and a wavefront sensing arm allowing Non-Common Path Aberration (NCPA) estimation and correction.   The ANDES coronagraph design achieves a contrast level of 3×10⁻³ at 20 mas, compliant with scientific requirements for exoplanet detection. This development represents a major step toward integrating high-contrast imaging and high-resolution spectroscopy on the ELT, bridging the gap between direct imaging and spectral characterization of exoplanets.

Items.Authors: Michael Weber, Daniel Sablowski, Ulrike Lemke, Katja Poppenhaeger, Julián D. Alvarado-Gómez, Svend-Marian Bauer, Olga Bellido-Tirado, Joar Brynnel, Frank Dionies, Domenico Giannone, Arto Järvinen, Silva Järvinen, Hakan Önel, Jörg Weingrill, Thomas Liebner, Michael Sigwarth, Falk Hoffmann, Markus Roth, Bruno Chazelas, Audrey Lanotte, Ludovic Genolet, Michael Sordet, Ian Hughes, Christophe Lovis, Yevgeniy Ivanisenko, Pedro Morales Sanchez, Manuel Amate Plasencia, Ruggero Piazzolla, Afrodisio Vega Moreno, Jonay I. González Hernández, Wolfgang Gaessler, Michael Lehmitz, Adrian Kaminski, Ingo Stilz, Paolo Di Marcantonio
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrograph for the ELT: the UBV spectrograph module
Items.Abstract: We present the design of the ANDES UBV module, the bluest spectrograph of the ANDES instrument. It is a fiber-fed high resolution, high stability spectrograph, which will be installed on the ELT-Nasmyth platform to minimize blue fibre losses from the focal plane to the spectrograph. In this paper we present the status of development of the spectrograph, its optical design, and auxiliary devices like exposure meter and leveling system, on its way to the final design stage. As stability is the prime design driver, a thermal enclosure is provided to keep temperature of the optical train stable at ambient conditions, the pressure is kept constant inside a vacuum vessel, and the leveling of the instrument is actively controlled. The science, sky background and simultaneous calibration light is fed to the spectrographs via fiber bundles of 66 fibres, which are arranged in a straight row forming the spectrograph slit.

Items.Authors: Paolo Picchi, Andrea Tozzi, Anna Brucalassi, Alen Khanbekyan, Ernesto Oliva, Monica Rainer
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrometer for the ELT: AIT/AIV activities on the Integral Field Unit subsystem
Items.Abstract: ANDES is a fibre-fed, high resolution (R=100000) spectrograph of the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT), with an observation band between 0.4 and 1.8 micron, with the possibility to extend it toward the U and K bands. ANDES has two observing modes: seeing-limited and Integral Field Unit (IFU), the last one available only in the YJH bands. The IFU mode concluded the sub-system Preliminary Design Review (PDR), and ANDES is progressing toward system level PDR. In this paper, we present the plan and development of the AIT and AIV activities regarding the IFU subsystem, providing details regarding the alignment and the performance verification of the most critical components of the instrument, such as: derotator, Atmospheric Dispersion Corrector (ADC) and the Alignment Check System (ACS) crucial to guarantee the performance of the instrument, especially in the most expanded zoom mode.

Items.Authors: Alen Khanbekyan, Andrea Tozzi, Anna Brucalassi, Monica Rainer, Alessandro Marconi, Ernesto Oliva
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrometer for the ELT: preliminary laboratory results of modal noise mitigation technics for the fibre injection system of the ANDES-IFU module
Items.Abstract: The ANDES instrument includes several fibre-fed high-resolution spectrographs covering 400–1800 nm. It offers two observing modes: a seeing-limited mode, where target light is injected directly into a large fibre, and an IFU mode, where the ELT focal plane is re-imaged at different spatial scales onto a microlens array feeding bundles of smaller fibres. In the seeing-limited mode, modal noise is controlled thanks to uniform illumination from natural seeing and fast tip-tilt mirrors. The IFU mode is more exposed to modal noise because the pupil entering each fibre is smaller than the fibre core—especially in the most expanded scale (~7 mas/spaxel), where it is about 18 times smaller. To reduce this, the IFU includes a fast XY piezo stage that moves the pupil during the exposure, improving illumination uniformity. We present preliminary measurements obtained with an ANDES-IFU prototype, testing different XY motions, fibre types, and agitation techniques.

Items.Authors: Davide Savio
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrometer for the ELT: quantifying the scientific impact of modal noise through laboratory-driven end-to-end simulations
Items.Abstract: Modal noise in multimode fibres is a significant source of systematic error for next-generation fibre-fed spectrographs such as ANDES for the ESO-ELT. We present a study that combines controlled laboratory experiments with end-to-end simulations to quantify its impact on instrument performance. Laboratory measurements under different fibre configurations and illumination conditions provide empirical constraints on the temporal and spectral behaviour of modal noise. These results are used to build an empirical modal-noise model integrated into a simulator of ANDES observations. As a case study, we evaluate the effect on exoplanet transmission spectroscopy, showing that modal noise can reduce detection significance and must be mitigated at the hardware level. The study provides quantitative guidance for defining acceptable modal-noise levels during ANDES design.

Items.Authors: Alessio Turchi, Andrea Tozzi, Alen Khanbekyan, Ernesto Oliva, Davide Savio, Monica Rainer
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrometer for the ELT: statistical description of modal noise in multimode fibers
Items.Abstract: Modal noise in multimode fibers represents a significant challenge for high-precision radial velocity measurements in upcoming spectrographs. ANDES (ArmazoNes high Dispersion Echelle Spectrograph), the first-light high-res spectrograph at the Extremely Large Telescope, has an ambitious goal of ~10 cm/s radial velocity precision, thus mitigating this noise is critical. Modal noise originates from the interference of different propagation modes and translates into wavelength-dependent fluctuations that produce spurious shifts in spectral line positions. This can  mask genuine Doppler signals from exoplanets or stellar activity. In this contribution we present a characterization of modal noise in multimode fibers and investigate if diffusion models from statistical mechanics can be effective in its description. Our analysis provides new insights into the fundamental behavior of modal noise and its impact on spectroscopic stability, and allows to evaluate potential mitigation techniques.

Items.Authors: Andrea Tozzi, Anna Brucalassi, Simone D'Auria, Alen Khanbekyan, Paolo Picchi, Ernesto Oliva, Fabio D'Anca, Monica Rainer, Marcello Scalera, Enrico Giro, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Veronica Baldini, Matteo Porru, Alessandro Marconi
Items.Title: ANDES, the high-resolution spectrometer for the ELT: towards the final design of the Integral Field Unit
Items.Abstract: ANDES (ArmazoNes high Dispersion Echelle Spectrograph) is the high-resolution spectrograph for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope, providing unprecedented spectroscopic capabilities in the optical and near-infrared range. The Integral Field Unit (IFU) module has passed its subsystem Preliminary Design Review (PDR), and ANDES is progressing towards system-level PDR. We present the finalized optical design and tolerance analysis results, ensuring required performance across the operational range. The zoom system for spaxel definition, allowing adaptive spatial sampling optimization, is detailed with its implementation strategy. We describe the Alignment Check System (ACS), critical for maintaining optical alignment and performance verification. The mechanical design is presented, including structural architecture and thermal management. Motion control systems enabling IFU reconfiguration are outlined, providing operational flexibility for diverse scientific programs.

Items.Authors: Sebastiaan van der Tol
Items.Title: Application of continuous corrections in wide‑field imaging obtained with the IDG‑CAL calibration method
Items.Abstract: Wide field observations by interferometric radio telescopes are affected by direction dependent instrumental and atmospheric effects. IDG-CAL is a method to estimate corrections that are continuous over the image directly from the visibilities. Continuous corrections are a closer match to reality than piece wise constant corrections in facets based methods. We demonstrate this technique on a number of LOFAR observations.

Items.Authors: Danielle N. Gurgew
Items.Title: Application of gold release layers for the fabrication of high-angular resolution, replicated full-shell X-ray optics
Items.Abstract: Achieving sub-arcsecond angular resolution with NiCo replicated full-shell optics necessitates improvements to the fabrication process, most notably release from the optical mandrel. Traditionally, NASA Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC) has used a passivation layer to facilitate this step, however, as resolution requirements become tighter, further optimization is required. Thin gold films deposited onto the mandrel before plating have shown promise in reducing errors through initial tests performed on both flat coupons and a small 62mm diameter mandrel. A second, more optically precise mandrel is used in this work to further validate these results by fabricating two shells, one with an optimized Au release layer, and one with the passivation layer. X-ray tests performed at MSFC’s 100m beamline are used to compare performance of the two full-shell optics, further quantifying the Au release layer’s effect on full-shell optical performance.

Items.Authors: Umi Enokidani, Go Murakami, Atsushi Yamazaki, Shingo Kameda, Masato Kagitani, Fuminori Tsuchiya, Ayaka Tadokoro
Items.Title: Application of the high-reflectivity ultraviolet coating for LAPYUTA to gratings
Items.Abstract: We are developing high-reflectivity mirrors to improve the detection efficiency of the focal plane instruments aboard LAPYUTA, a Japanese UV telescope that was selected as one of candidates of JAXA’s M-class mission. For one of LAPYUTA's primary science targets, the atomic oxygen emission line at 130.4 nm, the typical reflectivity of Al + MgF₂ mirrors remains around 85%. Therefore, improving each mirror reflectivity is essential to maintain high detection efficiency. We achieved 90% reflectivity on a flat substrate. Our next step is to apply this coating to gratings. LAPYUTA has two spectrographs: a medium-dispersion spectrograph with spectral resolution R ≈ 6,000, and a high-dispersion spectrograph with R ≈ 40,000. The current coatings reflectivity is 77% at 130 nm, and an absolute diffraction efficiency of 52%. If a coating with 90 % reflectivity can be deposited on the grating, the absolute diffraction efficiency is expected to increase to approximately 60 %.

Items.Authors: Federico Incardona, Alessandro Costa, Kevin Munari, Sebastiano Spinello, Emilio Mastriani
Items.Title: Architectural advancements of the Monitoring System for the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory
Items.Abstract: The CTAO Monitoring System (MON) architecture has been significantly advanced in the second ACADA (Array Control and Data Acquisition) release, completing the migration to the ACADA Configuration Database (aCDB) as the unified repository for all monitoring configurations.    In this release, monitoring data from the Large-Sized Telescopes (LSTs) are now exposed through OPC-UA servers, together with the set of auxiliary instruments foreseen for integration — including the weather station, stellar photometer, and external telescope calibration instrumentation. The updated MON also introduces new interfaces that extend its integration with the other ACADA submodules.    Extensive performance tests of the new MON version have been conducted both in a continuous integration environment, exploiting simulated monitoring points, and with the first operating LST in La Palma. The results confirm the scalability, robustness, and operational readiness of the upgraded architecture.

Items.Authors: Jiahao Zhou, Mengmeng Qian, Wenfei Liu, Yingfu Wang, Haoyang Zhang, Kai Yun, Xianke Song, Hongzhuan Hu, Jianping Wang, Jiaru Chu, Ping Zhang, Zhigang Liu, Zengxiang Zhou
Items.Title: Architecture Design and Implementation of a Closed-Loop Fiber Positioning Control System Based on ZeroMQ and CAN Bus
Items.Abstract: To meet the control demands of the upcoming large-scale focal plane upgrade for the LAMOST telescope, this research addresses the critical limitations of traditional centralized architectures in scalability and reliability. We propose and implement a novel distributed closed-loop control system for the Fiber Positioning Units. At its core is an innovative hybrid communication framework that effectively integrates high-level messaging with real-time fieldbus networks. Experimental validation confirms that the new system architecture achieves substantial improvements in stability, real-time performance, and scalability compared to the legacy system, providing a robust solution for future ultra-large-scale spectroscopic survey instruments.

Items.Authors: Emilie Bouzerand, Adrian M. Glauser, Marcel Baer, Paul Prantl, Werner Laun, Dirk Lesman, Ted Huang, Remko Stuik, Gert Raskin, Muhammad Salman
Items.Title: Assembly and testing of the cryostat for ELT/METIS
Items.Abstract: We present the cryostat of the Mid-infrared ELT Imager and Spectrograph (METIS) instrument to be operated at ESO’s Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). The cryostat holds the cold optics and mechanics of the instrument within the required cryo-vacuum environment. The radiation shields of the cryostat are cooled with liquid nitrogen while the cold subsystems are cooled via pulse-tube coolers down to temperatures between 35 K and 70 K. The cold-warm interface is provided with G10 blades that build together with the top part of the cryostat vessel the structural interface to the cold subsystems, the warm support structure, and the warm calibration source. The cryostat has been integrated and tested at ETH where it could be confirmed it fulfills the requirements. We present in this paper the final design, the key design considerations, highlights from the integration and testing phase and final performance.

Items.Authors: Vipin Kumar, Yigit Dallilar, Michael Wiest, Lucas Labadie, Adhirath Deshmukh, Margo Gassmüller, Tarun Kumar Sharma, Dennis Dolkens, Dirk Lesman, Remko Stuik, Adrian Glauser, Bernhard Brandl, Roy van Boekel, Wolfgang Brandner, Christian Staubmeier, Felix Bettonvil
Items.Title: Assembly, integration, and testing of the Warm Calibration Unit for METIS/ELT: optical performance verification and alignment procedures
Items.Abstract: Within the international METIS consortium, the University of Cologne is responsible for the design, manufacturing, integration, and qualification of the Warm Calibration Unit (WCU) subsystem of the instrument. This paper gives an overall view of the AIT phase of the WCU, describing the assembly and alignment operation on its CFRP bench. It focuses on the methods used to bring the subassemblies into their required positions, supporting our AIT workflow. It also provides an overview of the optical performance verification, describing the tests carried out to measure the key optical parameters. The paper also summarizes the opto-mechanical design and optical performance verification of the AIV optics. Finally, we describe the overall strategy for aligning the WCU to the Common For-Optics of the METIS instrument.

Items.Authors: Daniel J. Ahrer, M. Concepción Cárdenas Vázquez, Thomas Bertram, Peter Bizenberger, Armin Huber, Raphaël Pourcelot, Silvia Scheithauer, Horst Steuer
Items.Title: Assembly, integration, and verification of MITESI: an optical testbed for simulating the ELT in the laboratory
Items.Abstract: The MIni elt TElescope SImulator (MITESI) is an optical testbed, operating from λ = 1.50 - 2.42 µm and λ = 3.50 - 4.10 µm, which enables closed loop operations of a wavefront sensor in the laboratory.    In this contribution, we detail the use case and functionality of MITESI and explain how this is achieved on the optical bench by providing an overview of the optical layout. We go on to discuss the assembly and integration of MITESI in the laboratory. We conclude by detailing verification tests carried out to validate and demonstrate the performance of MITESI.

Items.Authors: Luís Sousa, Carlos Correia, Paulo Garcia
Items.Title: Assessing the astrometric and photometric performance of Starfinder2 in ELT METIS simulated images
Items.Abstract: METIS enables L’-band observations of red objects in stellar clusters and the Galactic Centre, but realistic astrometric and photometric error budgets are lacking. Using a METIS consortium simulation pipeline, ScopeSim, we generated images including field-varying AO PSFs, detector effects, and instrumental characteristics. We apply StarFinder2 to perform advanced source extraction and deblending while accounting for field-dependent variations. Initial tests with SExtractor revealed astrometric errors and a 150 μas precision limit. Starfinder2 is expected to improve these results and provide a more reliable error budget for METIS L’-band imaging.

Items.Authors: Amirhossein Kermani, Matteo Z. Genoni, Mercello Agostino Scalera, Marco Riva
Items.Title: AstroMBSE+: extending AstroMBSE methodology based on lessons learned from the CUBES Mission
Items.Abstract: ASTROMBSE methodology is the first MBSE methodology developed specifically for managing astronomical instrument projects. This methodology integrates the primary systems engineering processes, encompassing the management of Requirements, Interfaces, and the Product Breakdown Structure (PBS). In this study, we introduce ASTROMBSE+, an extended version of ASTROMBSE based on lessons learned from the CUBES instrument. Three main refinements are introduced: preserving the PBS code and a general PBS component pool, adding a verification step after the PBS generation phase, and simulating the CUBES maintenance procedures within the model. Overall, ASTROMBSE+ strengthens traceability, supports more reliable configuration control, and extends MBSE support and deployment beyond design into operations, enhancing the full lifecycle management, maintainability, and long-term evolution of a complex astronomical instrument project.

Items.Authors: Danièl N. Groenewald, Rudi Kuhn, Lee Townsend, Moses Mogotsi, Alexei Kniazev, Antoine Mahoro, Austun Louw, Veronica van Wyk, Nomzamo Makoena, Christian Hettlage, Nhlavutelo Macebele, Phelokazi Dube, Encarni Romero Colmenero, Lisa Crause, Rosalind Skelton, Anja Schroeder
Items.Title: Astronomy Operations with the Southern African Large Telescope
Items.Abstract: SALT is a 10-m class optical telescope located in Sutherland, South Africa. It is owned by an international consortium and operated in fully queue-scheduled mode by the South African Astronomical Observatory, which also manages several other national facilities.    In this paper, we present an updated overview of SALT’s performance, including key metrics such as completion rates, operational efficiency, and scientific output. We also discuss recent strategic developments and instrumentation updates implemented to further enhance the observatory’s performance and scientific impact.

Items.Authors: Xiaoyan Li, Yiqiao Yang
Items.Title: Auto guiding system with a slit in the spectrograph of a 1m telescope of Sitian Project
Items.Abstract: As a pilot node of the SiTian Project,the Wuhan University 1 m telescope is equipped with a low-resolution spectrograph. During long-duration spectroscopic observations, mechanical factors and environmental disturbances cause stellar image drift. This study discusses an auto-guiding system with a slit designed to compensate for this drift. The key techniques include image preprocessing, slit edge detection, star centroid extraction, and real-time axes decoupling. Specifically, the system employs a dual-channel feature decoupling algorithm to identify the slits and target stars. Furthermore, it addresses the nonlinear coupling of the control axes by constructing a coordinate transformation matrix based on the real-time parallactic angle.The experimental results demonstrate that the system stabilizes the target star within the 1 arcsecond slit, achieving a centroiding accuracy better than 0.01 pixels and an average processing time of less than 10 ms.

Items.Authors: Changyu Zeng, Teng Xu, Yue Sun, Wei Wei, Chao Liu, Junzhe Huang, Tao Wang, Xuhao Wu, Yonghui Hou, Xiangqun Cui
Items.Title: Auto-alignment and stabilization of the relay optics in long baseline optical interferometer
Items.Abstract: This work presents an auto-alignment system to stabilize long-baseline stellar interferometers against atmospheric and mechanical disturbances. Its two-stage architecture combines slow tip-tilt mirrors (guided by a position sensor) and fast tip-tilt mirrors (controlled by an EMCCD) to correct optical path drift. Testing on a simulated 70-m link under turbulence (single r₀ seeing) demonstrated sub-arcsecond RMS angular stabilization and extended fringe contrast stability to several hours.

Items.Authors: Patricia Van de Walle Suárez, Gilles Orban de Xivry, Olivier Absil, Valentin Christiaens, J. Markus Bonse, Robert J. De Rosa
Items.Title: Autodifferentiable PSF modeling for the VLT/ERIS vortex coronagraph
Items.Abstract: The Enhanced Resolution Imager and Spectrograph (ERIS) at the VLT is a second-generation mid-infrared imager and spectrograph, and a leading ground-based facility for high-contrast imaging, including a vortex coronagraph mode.    Although the vortex coronagraph provides small inner working angles and high throughput, direct imaging is still limited by residual starlight. To overcome this, we have developed a differentiable optical model of the ERIS vortex coronagraph, optimizing physical parameters via gradient-based methods to accurately reconstruct post-coronagraphic PSFs.    We are now incorporating real-time wavefront telemetry data to model and subtract evolving speckle noise, strengthening the approach for on-sky observations.     We present our framework and early proof-of-concept results using ERIS on-sky data and AO telemetry, demonstrating how model-based post-processing can enhance contrast near bright sources and pave the way for future facilities such as ELT/METIS.

Items.Authors: Gabriel E. Marinello, Juan Cortes
Items.Title: Automatic Astronomer Shift Scheduling in ALMA
Items.Abstract: As part of operational planning at ALMA, the Program Management Group (PMG) produces a quarterly schedule for Astronomers on Duty (AoD). Because the science staff dedicate only a fraction of their contracted time to AoD duties, constructing a schedule that satisfies complex constraints, including rest periods, vacations, and science leave, presents a significant operational challenge.    Historically, this task was performed manually, requiring at least one week of management effort and remaining highly error-prone. We addressed these issues by developing an automated solution capable of generating hundreds of candidate schedules within seconds.    We modeled the AoD scheduling as a Boolean Satisfiability (SAT) problem, a standard approach in Operations Research and Computer Science, and implemented the solver using Python and Google's OR-Tools.    In this talk, we describe the mathematical formalism, implementation, challenges, and avenues for future development.

Items.Authors: Enol Matilla Blanco
Items.Title: automatic temperature control loop for cryogenic detectors with beckhoff
Items.Abstract: Detectors in cryogen need to be heated and cool down at a specific maximum rate for safety.  Also, they need to stay above the optical bank temperature until a certain point to avoid possible condensation in the detector.  Because of that, we implemented a complete control loop on a Beckhoff PLC that manages all the changes on setpoints and ramps of the LakeShore 336 used to monitor and control the H2RG detector and ASIC of FRIDA.  This control loop also manage fails like helium compressor stops to maintain the detector at a safety temperature point.

Items.Authors: Ivan Cámara Mayorga, Pierre Bourget
Items.Title: Automatic tip-tilt adjustment system for the optical metrology delay lines at the VLT: enhancing performance and reducing operational costs
Items.Abstract: This work presents the development of an automatic tip-tilt adjustment system for the Delay Lines (DLs) optical metrology system, aimed at reducing corrective maintenance efforts and improving system performance. The project, pioneered and developed under the Integrated Operations Program (IOP) at ESO's VLT, addresses the complex challenges posed by environmental variations and the dynamic interactions between the DL rails and the moving carriage optics. These factors cause variations in the carriage trajectory, leading to metrology errors that often require frequent rail adjustments and complex corrections for hysteresis and wobble.  By implementing an innovative tip-tilt correction system acting on the Variable Curvature Mirror (VCM), we aim to significantly reduce rail adjustment and maintenance operations, as well as eliminate the need for manual hysteresis corrections. This system also enhances the metrology transfer function, resulting in better correction bandwidth.

Items.Authors: Roman Zoufal, Roland Ottensamer, Franz Kerschbaum, Gerald Moesenlechner, Armin Luntzer, Dominik Loidolt, Marko Mecina, Christopher Granabetter, Sam Kamptisch, Manuel Guedel, Antonio Rodriguez-Senin, Santiago Serrano, Timo Ruehl, Marco Sirianni
Items.Title: Autonomous guide star acquisition for Arrakihs
Items.Abstract: The guide star acquisition process for the Arrakihs Fine Guidance System (FGS) and its performance are presented in this contribution. The acquisition autonomously selects guide stars within the field of view, instead of relying on information pre-prepared on ground. The FGS measurements produced by the Arrakihs Common Data Processing Unit’s (CDPU) Instrument Application Software (IASW) are essential for achieving the unprecedented surface brightness targeted by the mission.

Items.Authors: Manuel Huertas López, Josué Toledo Castro, Ismael Álvarez Candelario, César Cabrera Rodríguez
Items.Title: Big Data Lakehouse Architecture for Advanced Analytics in Control Systems
Items.Abstract: Modern astronomical facilities generate large volumes of multivariate telemetry, whose systematic use is essential for predictive maintenance and reliable operations. This work presents a Lakehouse-based Big Data architecture that unifies heterogeneous observatory sources—including IIoT streams, control-system telemetry, meteorology, and logs—and enables both real-time and offline analytics. The platform integrates continuous ingestion with Apache Kafka, distributed processing with Spark Structured Streaming, and transactional storage with Apache Iceberg on S3-compatible object storage, governed by robust data-quality and metadata management. Machine-learning techniques are evaluated to detect anomalous behaviors at early stages, supporting predictive-maintenance workflows and providing a foundation for analytical digital-twin capabilities in large telescope facilities.

Items.Authors: Ranjani Srinivasan, Samantha Gray, Thomas Gauron, Ryan Chaves, Manuel Fernandez, Janice Houston, Michael Johnson, Rebecca Baturin, Jonathan Weintroub, Rurik Primiani, Kazunori Akiyama, Peter Galison, Daniel Marrone, Summer Franks, John Ford, Eli A. Zervigon, Ross Mpi, Stephen Joyce, Gilles Aminot, Doug Martens
Items.Title: Black Hole Explorer (BHEX) signal processing and instrument control electronics
Items.Abstract: The Black Hole Explorer is a new mission that will discover and measure a black hole’s photon ring, capturing light that has orbited a black hole. This paper describes the development of the backend electronics of the Black Hole Explorer (BHEX) instrument, which is called the “Signal Processing and Instrument Control Electronics” (SPICE).The functional and physical architecture are described with motivation for their design, including critical trades and design decisions made to satisfy the established SPICE requirements.

Items.Authors: Wen-Ping Chen, Ming-Hsin Chang, Yung-Hsin Chang, Ting-Wan Chen, Yi Chou, Daisuke Kinoshita, Chow-Choong Ngeow, Yen-Chen Pan, Anli Tsai, Lung-Ting Wang, Yair Krongold, Liliana Figueroa, Erica Lugo, Laurence Sabin
Items.Title: Bootstrapping transient astronomy with the Trans-Pacific 2-m Telescope
Items.Abstract: Summary of abstract for display in the program (119 words)    We describe the project to install the Trans-Pacific 2-m telescope facility at the San Pedro Mártir Observatory (SPM) in Mexico, a collaboration between NCU in Taiwan and UNAM in Mexico, together with other international partners. The facility is instrumented, with a simultaneous multiband imager and an efficient spectrograph, to optimize fast characterization of cosmic transient events recognized by, e.g., the LSST or SVOM, in synergy with other telescopes on the same site or in Taiwan. We describe the key parameters of the facility components, such as the telescope, instruments, robotic operations, time allocation and coordinated queue scheduling strategy, alert responses, the status of the project, and forward planning. The telescope is expected to see the first light in 2027.

Items.Authors: Michael Mann, Alessandro Priebsch, Alexander Stock, Thorsten Döhring, Udo Sauer, Georgios Fotis
Items.Title: Breaking the 10 minute barrier: transient recorder-based power quality diagnostics at astronomical observatories
Items.Abstract: Astronomical observatories, supplied via long stub‑line grids, are highly vulnerable to power quality (PQ) disturbances. Conventional monitoring based on 10‑minute averages misses fast transient events that degrade electromagnetic compatibility and the signal‑to‑noise ratio of sensitive instruments. We present a novel diagnostic concept: applying transient recorders, known from high‑voltage impulse testing, to PQ analysis. This enables massively parallel, microsecond‑scale measurements across phase, neutral, and protective earth conductors, revealing harmonics, coupling paths, and grounding deficiencies hidden to standard methods. Beyond observatories, the approach serves as a blueprint for decentralized “cellular” energy systems, supporting renewable integration and resilience. It aligns with international frameworks (IEC TR 63410, IEEE 519, IEC SyC Smart Energy) and extends the VDE cellular approach, bridging astrophysics and energy system transformation.

Items.Authors: Roisin Ryan, Charlotte Feldman, Alejandro Guzmán Cabrera, Lauro Conti, Anna Maskolenko, Paul R. Houghton, Gillian Butcher, Daniel Schuppe, Vadim Burwitz
Items.Title: Building and testing breadboard optics for the soft X-ray imager on the THESEUS mission
Items.Abstract: THESEUS (Transient High Energy Sources and Early Universe Surveyor) is a candidate in ESA’s M7 call, which aims to study high redshift Gamma ray bursts and transient X-ray events. The mission is currently in phase A, with proposed launch in 2037.  The Soft X-ray Imager (SXI) of the mission will consist of two lobster eye modules covering a field of view of 0.5sr. An array of micro-pore optics (MPOs) focuses the image of the soft X-ray sky to an array of CMOS detectors searching for transients in the 0.3-5 keV energy range.  A technology development activity (TDA) was commissioned by ESA to manufacture and perform metrology on frames of slightly varying materials and to charcterize with X-rays MPOs from different manufacturers.  The results, comparison and interpretation of the tests are presented in this work.

Items.Authors: Vincent Deo, Olivier Guyon, Jared Males, Katie Morzinski, Christoph Baranec, Michael Bottom, Rebecca Jensen-Clem, Nour Skaf, Avinash Surendran, Mark Chun
Items.Title: CACAO++: scheduling user experience as the core of adaptive optics RTCs
Items.Abstract: We report on our 3-year effort to redesign and expand the free and open-source Compute And Control for Adaptive Optics (CACAO) RTC toolkit for adaptive optics.  CACAO has long served as the core RTC system for SCExAO and MagAO-X and is now used at multiple facilities (MAPS, AO3k, ULTIMATE,...). CACAO offers a core realtime infrastructure based on high modularity and expandability, and we are continuously broadening its natively available computational features, integrating cutting edge algorithms and hardware accelerations per community needs.    This CACAO++ project targets three goals:  (1) improved usability via documentation, tutorials, visualization tools, simulation interfaces, and a new python configuration layer;  (2) improved collaboration through API refactoring, modern packaging, and CI/CD;  (3) enhanced performance in real-time resource management, HPC interfacing, and multi-node operation.    We invite community feedback/participation in shaping the future of open-source AO RTC
